limitations: Unverified apps are restricted to 100 test users and display an 'unverified app' consent warning screen.
Restricted scopes (e.g. Gmail full access, Google Drive) mandate a third-party CASA security assessment costing $15k-$75k/year.

missingEvidence: Exact human review turnaround variance during global holiday quarters.

assumptions: Developer has existing Google Cloud account with active billing account linked
OAuth consent screen requires only non-sensitive scopes (openid, email, profile)

prerequisites.text: Verified domain ownership in Google Search Console (if publishing to production)

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud Project & Enable APIs
steps.instructions: Navigate to the Google Cloud Console (console.cloud.google.com). In the top project selector dropdown, click 'New Project'. Provide a project name (e.g. 'My App OAuth') and click 'Create'. Once created, select the project from the notification bell.
steps.completionCheck: Project name appears in the top header breadcrumb.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen
steps.instructions: In the left navigation menu, go to 'APIs & Services' > 'OAuth consent screen'. Select User Type: 'External' (for multi-tenant/public users) or 'Internal' (Workspace users only). Enter App name, User support email, and Developer contact information. Click 'Save and Continue'.
steps.completionCheck: Consent screen status shows 'Testing' with user type configured.

steps.title: Select Scopes (Follow Least Privilege)
steps.instructions: On the 'Scopes' step, click 'Add or Remove Scopes'. Select non-sensitive scopes needed: `.../auth/userinfo.email`, `.../auth/userinfo.profile`, `openid`. Do not select sensitive or restricted scopes unless mandatory for your core value proposition.
steps.completionCheck: Scopes list shows only non-sensitive classification.

steps.title: Add Test Users (Testing Phase)
steps.instructions: While in 'Testing' mode, click 'Add Users' under the Test Users tab. Enter the Gmail or Google Workspace addresses of your developers/QA testers. Only these authorized accounts can sign in until verification or publishing.
steps.completionCheck: Test emails appear in the 'Test users' table.

steps.title: Create OAuth 2.0 Client ID Credentials
steps.instructions: Navigate to 'APIs & Services' > 'Credentials' > 'Create Credentials' > 'OAuth client ID'. Select Application type: 'Web application'. Add your Authorized JavaScript origins (e.g. `http://localhost:3000`, `https://app.example.com`) and Authorized redirect URIs (e.g. `https://app.example.com/api/auth/callback/google`). Click 'Create'.
steps.completionCheck: Modal pops up showing your Client ID and Client Secret.

blockers.title: Google Consent Screen 'App Not Verified' Warning
blockers.description: External apps requesting sensitive scopes show a deceptive red warning banner to end users unless they pass Google Brand & Scope Verification.

blockers.title: Domain Verification Prerequisite
blockers.description: Before Google approves an app branding logo or privacy policy URL, the root domain must be verified via DNS TXT record in Google Search Console under the same developer email.

claims.text: Every OAuth client requires an active Google Cloud Project container.
Internal user type restricts login to users inside your Google Workspace organization, bypassing external app verification.
Apps in Testing publishing status are capped at 100 designated test accounts.
Email, profile, and openid scopes are classified as non-sensitive and do not require video submission or manual app review.
Redirect URIs must match exact string characters including protocol, trailing slash, and port in development.

selectedPassages: To use OAuth 2.0 in your application, you need an API console project to obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials and create a client ID.
Redirect URIs are the endpoints to which the OAuth 2.0 server can send responses.
Unverified apps face quota restrictions and display an unverified app screen to users before authorization.
Brand verification reviews typically conclude within 3-7 business days.
